newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ends probe of STET activity in Cuba.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ends probe of STET activity in Cuba.

text.p: The U.S. State Department said Wednesday it had ended "without adverse action" an investigation into use of confiscated property in Cuba by Italian telecommunications company STET International.

Spokesman Nicholas Burns said the decision was taken after ITT Corporation informed the department it had reached an agreement with STET on the Italian company's use of ITT's confiscated property in Cuba.
Burns said ITT had told the department that in return for a one-time payment by STET it was authorizing the company to do what it wished with the Cuban Telephone System, formerly owned by ITT.

The department had decided that this meant that STET was not violating a section of the U.S. Helms-Burton law, which provides for senior executives of companies deemed to be "trafficking" in property seized from U.S. nationals in Cuba to be barred from the United States.

"The Department has, therefore, terminated without adverse action the investigation which had been ongoing related to STET International's and its affiliates' use of ITT's confiscated property in Cuba," Burns said in a written statement.
He said the Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control had reviewed the STET-ITT agreement and issued a license to ITT to authorize it to implement the accord.
